provenance: M31. `agent.plan_gap` is a pure function over (task text, plan) and the two end-to-end cases only reach two of its rows: `verifier-aggregate-superlative-fails-loud` (aggregate task, no enumerating step -> rejected before any action) and `probe3-quotes-most-quoted-author` (the same, replanned into an enumeration that answers correctly). This is the table underneath them. The rows that matter and that neither E2E case reaches are the ones where the plan reads the page more than once. TWO `extract_all` steps produce a list of lists as the answer. ONE `extract_all` beside a plain `extract` is worse and was the M31 spec-drift audit's top finding against this function's first version, which asked only whether SOME step enumerated: on `quotes.html` the plan `[extract heading, extract_all links]` for "which author has the most quotes" ran to `status: success`, `verdict: PASS`, every L1 check green, with the answer `["Quotes Fixture", ["Login", "Tags", "Albert Einstein", ...]]` — an unranked candidate list, composite with the page heading, offered as the answer to a "which one" question. `verifier.rank` never sees it (it reduces an enumeration only when the enumeration is the whole answer) and the relaxed `aggregate_needs_comparison` check has no reason to reject a trace that does carry an enumeration. The rule is now "read the page exactly once, with `extract_all`", which makes zero, two, and one-plus-one the same gap. The non-aggregate rows are the other direction: the lint must not fire on an ordinary task however many enumerations its plan carries, or every list-shaped task starts replanning. T-M40-2 adds the lint's second rule (ADR-024) to the same table, because it is the same pure function: an extraction aimed at the accessibility document root is refused whatever the task shape, in every spelling a plan can name the ROOT with — padded and case-folded, but NOT ARIA `document`, which is an author-supplied role on an in-page container that Playwright resolves — and for `extract_all` as well as `extract` — enumerating a root produces one dump, not a set. The rows this table owns and the end-to-end case cannot reach are the two boundaries. The non-aggregate one is the placement itself: `plan_gap` opens with `if not is_aggregate(task): return None`, so a clause written below that line is dead for every ordinary task, which is what all five re-probed live tasks are. The `observe`/`click` rows are the other boundary and they are load-bearing in the opposite direction — M32's drill-down names a container ON PURPOSE (ADR-020), so a rule about the role alone would refuse the feature; the rule is about the action and the role together. No other case in the suite reaches an `observe` onto a root.

triage.note: tagged invariant, and watched red as an 'unknown invariant check plan-gap' error before the check existed — the same way inv3-budget-exhaustion-loud was. Watched red twice more against the first implementation of the lint, which asked `any(... == 'extract_all')`: the two-enumeration row and both one-plus-one orderings reported `expected_gap: true, got: null`. Watched red a fourth time for the T-M40-2 rows, before the ADR-024 clause existed: six rows `expected_gap: true, got: null` — the root spellings on a plain task, the `extract_all`-on-a-root row under the aggregate task (which the aggregate rule is content with: exactly one enumeration, `rank: true`), and the plain-plus-root two-step. Watched red a fifth time in the other direction, against the clause's FIRST version, which had ARIA `document` in the set: the two `document` rows reported `expected_gap: false` against a reason string asserting that an in-page container was "the ENTIRE page", and the padded-spelling row (` WebArea `) reported `expected_gap: true, got: null` — the set was case-folded but not stripped. Both came from the cold review of this change. The `observe`/`click` rows and the no-role rows were green before the clause and stayed green after, which is the assertion they exist to make.
